subject: Velociti load-pattern discovery & sizing clarification
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Velociti load-pattern discovery & sizing clarification

Hi Lena / Velociti infra team,

Great sync today — quick written recap and three clarifying asks so we can size a pilot/proposal:

What we heard on the call
- Endpoint: low-latency chat API (prompt -> assistant reply). Streaming of partial tokens is required for UI responsiveness.
- Conversation length: median ~350 tokens, 95th ~1,200 tokens.
- Baseline QPS: ~2–3 QPS (steady), Peak QPS sustained for short windows: 80–110 QPS (typically 5–10 minute crests during product events).
- Concurrent active sessions estimate at peak: ~150–220.
- Current observed p95 latency (internal infra): ~1.2s. Target for product: p95 <= 700ms, p50 <= 200ms.

Priyom's immediate sizing questions (please send back the CSV/log sample if available):
1) Can you share a 24‑hour request trace (timestamps, request token count, response token count) — CSV is fine. This will let us map tokens/sec to aggregate throughput and batching efficiency.
2) Streaming behavior: do you reliably need partial frames every 200–400ms for UI? Or is batched non-streaming acceptable for longer replies?
3) Any hard SLOs for tail latency (p99) or regional routing constraints?

Proposed next steps
- You: send token trace + confirm streaming cadence (ask 1 & 2).
- Redwood: we’ll run a quick cost/slot estimate and propose a pilot config (reserved pool + streaming tuning).
- Schedule: technical deep dive (30–45m) with Hannah (runtime) and Marissa (solutions) — propose Fri 12 Jun or Mon 15 Jun.

Attached: notes from today’s call (call-notes-velociti-20260609.pdf).

Thanks,
Priyom

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@velociti.ai>

Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Velociti load-pattern discovery & sizing clarification

Thanks Priyom — attaching the CSV we discussed.

Quick answers inline:
- Attachment: velociTi_token_trace_20260608.csv (columns: timestamp, req_tokens, resp_tokens, user_id, edge_region). Note: we scrubbed PII.
- Streaming: yes — our frontend shows a big UX improvement when we get token chunks every ~250ms. Full non-streaming is a fallback but will degrade perceived latency for long responses.
- Peak windows: event-driven spikes typically 5–10 minutes long, QPS hits ~90–120 during those crests. Outside those events we see 1.5–3 QPS.
- Concurrency: active sessions (socket connected + generating) ~160–220 at peak; most sessions are short (1–3 turns).
- Current infra p95: ~1.1–1.3s across regions. We’d like to get down to ~600–700ms p95 with Redwood.

We can also share a short 2‑hour high-fidelity trace if that helps.

—Lena

Subject: RE: Velociti load-pattern discovery & sizing clarification — internal next steps

Priyom / Hannah — quick internal read of Lena's CSV and the asks. Summary and recommended pilot:

What the trace shows (high level)
- Heavy long-tail on response tokens (median ~340, mean pulled up by occasional 1k+ replies).
- Burst cadence matches product events — several 7–12 minute crests where QPS jumps ~40–60x baseline.

Recommended pilot configuration (our proposal to Velociti)
1) Reserved pool to cover steady-state concurrency + a burst policy for crests (we can size initial reserved GPUs for ~200 concurrent sessions with aggressive batching and enable autoscale/burst for crests).
2) Streaming-enabled runtime with smaller token flush windows (~200–300ms) to meet perceived latency goals.
3) Target SLOs for pilot: p50 <= 200ms, p95 <= 700ms, p99 <= 1.5s (we'll instrument tracing to verify).

Data/ops checklist to finalize sizing (what we need from Velociti)
- 24‑hr request trace (we have an initial CSV but would like one full-day unaggregated).
- Confirmation that streaming cadence ~250ms is acceptable for the client.
- Any regional weightings (are 80% of requests west US?).
- A small subset of traffic (2 hours) we can route to a pilot cluster for live profiling.

I'll draft a short pilot checklist and a quick estimate mapping tokens/sec -> GPU-equivalent slots. Attaching the checklist now (pilot-checklist.xlsx).

If Hannah is available, she should join the Friday deep dive to talk kernel/latency tradeoffs and batching knobs.

—Marissa
